authority.legal_name: Şehir Hatları A.Ş., the public ferry operator owned by the Istanbul Metropolitan Municipality (İBB)
authority.geography_type: a strait city straddling two continents, with strong currents and dense shipping
authority.home_waters_label: the Bosphorus, the Golden Horn and the Sea of Marmara

mandate.summary: Şehir Hatları — City Lines — is the historic public ferry operator owned by the Istanbul Metropolitan Municipality. Its network crosses the Bosphorus between Europe and Asia, runs up the Golden Horn, and reaches out across the Sea of Marmara to the Princes' Islands, serving tens of millions of commuter, island and visitor journeys a year from more than fifty piers.
current_priorities: Run the cross-Bosphorus, Golden Horn and Princes' Islands ferry network from 50+ piers
Deliver the Istanbul Metropolitan Municipality electric-ferry program — new battery-electric vapur entering the fleet
Modernise the historic piers and integrate ticketing with the city's Istanbulkart network
Sustain the commuter, island and visitor mix across a city of more than 15 million people

policy_targets.vision: Istanbul Metropolitan Municipality (İBB) electric-ferry & clean-transport program; Türkiye 2053 net-zero target
policy_targets.decarb_note: The Istanbul Metropolitan Municipality is bringing battery-electric ferries into the Şehir Hatları fleet, modernising the historic vapur service toward the city's clean-transport goals.
policy_targets.relevance: Navier is the zero-emission, software-defined passenger-only foiling layer above the Şehir Hatları network — fast, low-wake hops across the Bosphorus and out to the Princes' Islands that complement the city's own electrification, with conventional low-speed handling in the busy Eminönü and Golden Horn approaches.

precedent.headline: Şehir Hatları runs the historic Istanbul ferry network — 50+ piers across two continents, tens of millions of journeys a year — and the city is now electrifying the fleet.
precedent.network: Lines cross the Bosphorus (Eminönü – Kadıköy – Üsküdar – Beşiktaş), run the Bosphorus villages up to Anadolu Kavağı, climb the Golden Horn to Eyüp, and reach the Princes' Islands (Büyükada, Heybeliada, Burgazada, Kınalıada) across the Sea of Marmara.
precedent.note: Public ferry service is core transport infrastructure here, not a novelty. Navier adds a fast passenger-only foiling layer on the busy corridors.

interpretation_for_navier: Navier is the zero-emission, software-defined passenger-only foiling layer above the Şehir Hatları network — fast, low-wake hops across the Bosphorus and out to the Princes' Islands that complement the city's own electrification, with conventional low-speed handling in the busy Eminönü and Golden Horn approaches.

domestic_pairs.rationale: The flagship cross-Bosphorus commute — Eminönü on the European shore to Kadıköy on the Asian shore.
Eminönü to Üsküdar across the Bosphorus mouth — the shortest, busiest continent-to-continent hop.
Karaköy to Kadıköy — a heavy cross-strait commute from the European waterfront.
Beşiktaş to Üsküdar — a core cross-Bosphorus commute crossing.
Beşiktaş to Kadıköy — a busy European-to-Asian commute line.
Eminönü up the full Bosphorus to Anadolu Kavağı — the classic strait line past the villages and fortresses.
Kabataş across the Sea of Marmara to Büyükada — the main Princes' Islands run.
Bostancı on the Asian shore to Büyükada — the short Princes' Islands crossing.
Üsküdar up the Golden Horn to Eyüp — the historic Haliç line.
Büyükada to Heybeliada — the inter-island hop in the Princes' Islands.

regional_links.note: The Şehir Hatları network is entirely domestic within Istanbul's waters — the Bosphorus, the Golden Horn and the Sea of Marmara to the Princes' Islands. There are no international legs; the whole proposal is domestic.

routing_hazards.instruction: Every domestic leg must be routed through navigable open water with NO land crossings (interior_land_km == 0). Hand-curated waypoints required wherever a breakwater, barrier, bridge pier, reef, headland, naval/exclusion zone or shallows would otherwise be clipped. Use data-clean/uae_hand_waypoints.json format {from, to, waypoints:[[lng,lat]...]}.

hazards.detail: The Bosphorus runs a strong surface current with a reverse counter-current beneath; hand-waypoint the crossings and account for the set on every continent-to-continent leg.

hazards.hazard: One of the world's busiest shipping straits
hazards.detail: The Bosphorus carries heavy commercial and tanker traffic under a traffic-separation scheme; cross-strait legs must cross the lanes perpendicular and route clear of the through-traffic.
The Princes' Islands legs cross open Marmara water exposed to wind and swell; route the marked crossings and manage exposure.
The Galata, Atatürk and Haliç metro bridges constrain the Golden Horn; route through the marked openings with air-draft and pier clearance.
Southerly lodos storms and Bosphorus fog reduce conditions in winter; routing and speed must respect closure advisories.
Eminönü, Karaköy, Üsküdar and Kadıköy are extremely busy ferry and fishing-boat piers; geofence speed and give-way behaviour on the approaches.
